title: RNN in PyTorch ⚙️
description: Use nn.RNN with proper input shapes, hidden state, and batching.

slides.title: The `nn.RNN` Module 📦
slides.content:
# Built‑in Recurrence

PyTorch provides `nn.RNN(input_size, hidden_size, num_layers=1)`. It processes the whole sequence in one call!

Input: `(L, N, H_in)` where:
* `L` = sequence length
* `N` = batch size
* `H_in` = input feature size

Output: `(L, N, H_out)` and the final hidden state `(num_layers, N, H_out)`.

slides.title: Using nn.RNN
slides.content: Create and run a simple RNN.
slides.codeSnippet:
rnn = nn.RNN(input_size=10, hidden_size=20, num_layers=1)
x = torch.randn(5, 2, 10)  # seq_len=5, batch=2, features=10
out, hn = rnn(x)
print(out.shape)   # [5, 2, 20]
print(hn.shape)    # [1, 2, 20]

quizData.question: For `nn.RNN(10, 20)` with input (7, 4, 10), what is the shape of the output?
quizData.explanation: Output preserves time and batch dimensions, changes feature size to hidden_size.

slides.title: Multi‑Layer RNNs 🏗️
slides.content:
## Stacking RNNs

`num_layers=2` stacks two RNNs: the output of the first becomes the input to the second.

* Input shape same, but `hidden_size` of first becomes `input_size` of second (usually same `hidden_size`).
* `hn` shape becomes `(num_layers, batch, hidden_size)`. The last layer's hidden state is often used for classification.

slides.title: Stacked RNN Example
slides.codeSnippet:
rnn2 = nn.RNN(10, 20, num_layers=2)
x = torch.randn(3, 1, 10)
out, hn = rnn2(x)
print(out.shape)  # [3, 1, 20]
print(hn.shape)   # [2, 1, 20]

quizData.question: For a 3-layer RNN, what does `hn` represent?

options.text: Only the last layer's hidden state
The output of the first layer

quizData.explanation: hn stacks the final hidden states of all layers, shape (num_layers, batch, hidden_size).

slides.title: Customizing Initial Hidden State 🧹
slides.content:
## Starting from Scratch

By default, hidden state is initialized to zeros. You can pass `h0` as an argument: `out, hn = rnn(x, h0)`. This is useful for continuing a sequence.

slides.title: Providing Initial h0
slides.content: Pass a specific initial hidden state.
slides.codeSnippet:
h0 = torch.randn(1, 2, 20)  # num_layers, batch, hidden
out, hn = rnn(x, h0)
print(hn.shape)  # [1, 2, 20]
